findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11(Q) Person In Charge. 11/13 inspection occurred as a result of confirmation of a falsified certified food manager certification present at the facility. Originally noted during the 11/12/26 inspection, inspector reached-out to SCDPH and ServSafe due to observation of the unique nature of the certificate. SCDPH observes 100s of certificates a year and this one presented with obvious doctored content. Upon confirmation, ServSafe did issue a certification to the individual in question, the certificate number and the expiration date are correct. The certificate given, however, is a false document that initially was issued to an employee Chase X. Someone doctored the available document. SCDPH recourse is to issue a follow-up to allow time for the facility to obtain proper certificates. 


The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (Q) Written procedures and plans, where specified by this Code and as developed by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, are maintained and implemented as required.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: During the 11/12 inspection, the certification presented appeared to be doctored. Upon investigation, the document presented was not for the correct person. McDonald’s has a fantastic in-house certification process and there are traditionally multiple CFPM present. Yesterday, the manager present did not indicate that anyone besides the single present party was certified. Be sure to educate managers that conversations with inspectors are key to good evaluations. If another certified person was present, this should have been indicated. Certified persons are present today.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed multiple TCS items to be held past their 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, items included biscuits and gravy, sweet tea, and Canadian bacon. Education was provided and items were discarded. Ensure any TCS item is discarded after 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Observed in use McRib utensil to be resting on a soiled tray. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper in use utensil storage and a new tray and utensil were used. Ensure any in use utensil is stored in a way that prevents any contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Observed walk in freezer fan unit to have ice accumulation present around hose. Discussed with PIC, unit will be serviced. Ensure staff is checking walk in freezer unit regularly to prevent any ice accumulation from building up.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed food debris/accumulation in the following areas:
1) (Repeatx2) The 2 door fry freezer was observed soiled with food debris. 
2) Small grease buildup on the floor near grills. 

Discussed with PIC, areas will be cleaned. Ensure non food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency that prevents any possible contamination. 



Discussed with PIC, areas will be cleaned. Ensure staff is cleaning non food contact surfaces at a frequency that prevents food accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Garbage and refuse are properly disposed; facilities are maintained.
findings.comment: Observed significant amount of refuse to be present behind washing machines. Discussed with PIC, area will be cleaned. Ensure any refuse is properly disposed of within facility.
findings.citation_text: 5-502.11 Frequency. REFUSE, recyclables, and returnables shall be removed from the PREMISES at a frequency that will minimize the development of objectionable odors and other conditions that attract or harbor insects and rodents.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed mop to be stored in mop bucket with soiled mop water present. Discussed with PIC, mop water will be discarded and mop will be stored in a way that allows for air drying. Ensure mop is stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.
